Title: Evaluation of requests for evaluation of the need for a full MRL evaluation for chemical-unlike biologicals

Procedure scope: The procedure covers the evaluation of 'chemical-unlike' biological substances in accordance with Commission Regulation (EU) 2018/782 to determine if a 'no MRL required' classification is appropriate without a full MRL evaluation. Definitions: Definitions are provided for key roles involved in the application process, including the Applicant, PC, CVMP Committee for Veterinary Medicinal Products, and various support roles (P3). Process flow: A process map outlines the steps from appointing a procedure team and rapporteur to the evaluation phase, including validation steps (P4). Pre-submission phase: The pre-submission phase involves receiving the letter of intent, appointing the team, and notifying the applicant of the appointed rapporteur and submission dates. Title: Evaluation procedure for applications and requests for the establishment or review of Maximum Residue Limits (MRLs)
Post Text: European Medicines Agency Evaluation procedure for applications and requests for the establishment or review of Maximum Residue Limits (MRLs) This guidance outlines the evaluation procedure for applications and requests concerning the establishment or review of Maximum Residue Limits (MRLs) under Regulation (EC) No 470/2009. Applicant definition: An applicant is defined as a person submitting an application for MRLs under Article 3, 10, or 15 of Regulation (EC) No 470/2009, which also includes Member States or the European Commission when submitting requests under Articles 9, 11, or 27. Procedure timelines: Timelines for accelerated procedures are specified in brackets following standard procedure timelines, such as 120 (90) days. Responsibility assignment: The Head of the Veterinary Evaluation and Innovation Support Department is responsible for ensuring adherence to the procedure within their department or service; execution responsibility is detailed in section 9. Pre-submission steps: The pre-submission phase involves checking a checklist, appointment of rapporteurs, agreeing on a start date, and validation. Initial evaluation timeframe: The initial evaluation must occur within 120 (90) days following procedural steps described in the checklist. Initial evaluation monitoring: Monitoring is required for the timely receipt of draft assessment reports, critiques, and comments from peer reviewers and CVMP members. Second evaluation conclusion: The conclusion of the second evaluation phase involves agreeing on the need for an oral explanation by the CVMP at Day 180 (119). Re-examination request: A notification to request re-examination must be received within a 15-day deadline to proceed to the next steps. Post Text: European Medicines AgencyOrganisation of CVMP Working Party meetings Applies to: Veterinary Medicines Division This guidance outlines procedures for the organisation and communication surrounding CVMP Working Party meetings, including roles, scheduling, and documentation management. Working Party Structure: The CVMP structure includes several Working Parties such as the Novel Therapies and Technologies Working Party (NTWP), Pharmacovigilance Working Party (PhVWP-V), Safety Working Party (SWP-V), and Scientific Advice Working Party (SAWP-V) (P2). Meeting Booking: Physical meeting room bookings must be made one year in advance, and meeting patterns should align with established patterns for different working parties. Meeting Request Timing: A meeting request should be submitted 8-4 weeks before the meeting for physical meetings, and virtual meeting setups require a Teams link. Participant Numbers: Participant numbers vary significantly across Working Parties, with PhVWP-V having 35 participants and SAWP-V having 16 participants (P4). Declaration of Interest: A check for the Declaration of Interest (DoI) status of all Working Party members and experts must be performed using the Expert Management Tool (EMT) before sending invitations. Invitation Timing: Invitations for physical meetings should be sent at the latest 8 weeks before the meeting, while virtual invitations can be sent up to 3 weeks in advance. First Mailing: The first mailing should be sent two weeks before the meeting, with documents indicated as 'To be circulated' if not yet available. Final Documentation: The final documentation package, including the final agenda, is tabled in the Meeting Management System (MMD) and made available to WP members after the meeting. Post Text: FDA SOPP 8212: Breakthrough Therapy Products - Designation and Management This SOPP covers rescinding designation, rescind criteria, periodic reviews. Rescinding Designation: The process involves notifying senior management that the product development program no longer meets the criteria for breakthrough therapy designation, and an Intent to Rescind letter will be issued to the sponsor. Rescind Criteria: CBER may rescind the designation if the sponsor fails to submit additional justification or supportive data or request a meeting within 60 days of receiving the Intent to Rescind letter. Periodic Reviews: Periodic reviews must occur at least annually to assess the continued adequacy of the proposed overall product development plan to support an expedited development program. Review Team Composition: The review team should involve senior managers and experienced staff in a collaborative, cross-disciplinary review, assigning a project lead to facilitate the review. Meeting Planning: Multidisciplinary meetings should include the proposed timing and frequency of future meetings, information requests, and submissions related to the product development program. Data Requirements: Required data includes the status of clinical trials, preliminary evidence of effectiveness, and safety profiles across various systems. PK/PD Data: Specific requirements include justification for dose selections, information on specific populations, and clinical pharmacology, pharmacodynamic, and pharmacokinetic trials. Nonclinical Strategy: Nonclinical strategies cover completed and planned studies, including toxicology, genetic toxicology, and manufacturing process comparisons. Title: SOPP 8215: Management of Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy Products: Request for Designation, Sponsor Interactions, and Status Assessment
Post Text: FDA SOPP 8215: Management of Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy Products: Request for Designation, Sponsor Interactions, and Status Assessment This SOPP outlines the procedures for managing Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) Products, detailing the framework for supporting and monitoring the accelerated development of regenerative therapies while maintaining rigorous eligibility standards. RMAT Scope: The SOPP covers procedures for reviewing requests for RMAT designation submitted via an IND or amendment, requests to withdraw designation, related meetings, and periodic summary reviews for the designation. RMAT Eligibility: A regenerative medicine therapy must be a cell therapy, tissue engineering product, human cell/tissue product, or combination product, and must target serious/life-threatening conditions with preliminary evidence of addressing unmet needs. Submission Rules: Sponsors may request RMAT designation with an IND or amendment, ideally by the end-of-phase 2 meeting. Decision Timeline: CBER will notify the sponsor within 60 calendar days regarding whether the RMAT designation has been granted. New Request Criteria: If a request is denied due to insufficient evidence, submitting new clinical data constitutes a new designation request; sponsors may request reconsideration based on the denial rationale within 60 days. IND Amendments Review: IND amendments related to RMAT products receive expedited review, generally within 60 days, unless statutory or regulatory exceptions apply. Designation Rescission: CBER may rescind designation if criteria are no longer met; sponsors have 60 days to submit additional justification or request a meeting to support continuation. Development Communication: CBER communicates with sponsors outside critical milestone meetings to provide intensive, discipline-focused guidance on development data and milestones. Title: Safety Reporting in clinical trials
Post Text: Swissmedic Safety Reporting in clinical trials This guidance covers susar reporting, atmp definition, susar criteria. SUSAR Reporting: All Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions (SUSARs) in clinical trials of categories B and C at Swiss trial centres must be reported to Swissmedic. This requires fulfilling three criteria: serious, related, and unexpected based on the Reference Safety Information [RSI]. Notification must include a completed submission form and a CIOMS form with participant details, medication information,, ATMP definition: ATMPs include transplant products, gene therapy products, and other nucleic acid-based products, and also products where genetic information is introduced into somatic cells, such as oligonucleotides, vectors, mRNA (including vaccines), and antisense RNA. SUSAR criteria: A Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) requires the fulfillment of three criteria: seriousness, relatedness, and unexpectedness based on the Reference Safety Information (RSI). SUSAR relatedness: In clinical trials with ATMPs, relatedness extends beyond the ATMP itself to include interventions associated with it, such as events during donation or administration. Comparator reporting: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions associated with comparator products or placebos follow the same reporting requirements as the test Investigational Medicinal Product (IMP). SUSAR timelines: Fatal and life-threatening SUSARs require initial notification within 7 days, with a follow-up report within 8 days after initial notification. Urgent safety measures: Sponsors must immediately report new events that could put trial participant safety at risk and report urgent safety measures (USMs) within 7 working days if permitted radiation dose guidance values are exceeded. Annual safety reports: Annual List of Events and Deficiencies or DSURs must include new SUSARs and an updated statement from the Sponsor on the benefit/risk ratio of the trial. Title: Clinical trials for medicines: modifying a clinical trial approval
Post Text: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency Clinical trials for medicines: modifying a clinical trial approval This guidance outlines the framework for modifying clinical trial approvals, categorising modifications and detailing the application processes for substantial changes. Modification Types: Clinical trial approvals may be modified by the sponsor, licensing authority, or ethics committee, with modifications categorised as substantial, important detail, or minor. Substantial Modifications: Substantial modifications are divided into Route A and Route B, with Route A modifications assessed based on impact on participant safety or data reliability. Route A Criteria: Route A substantial modifications include changes to primary/secondary endpoints with significant impact on safety or scientific value, or changes to the Investigational Medicinal Product (IMP) formulation or dosing. Minor Modifications: Minor modifications may be implemented at any time without informing the licensing authority or ethics committee at the point of implementation. Safety Data Changes: Modifications involving new toxicological data or interpretations that impact the risk and benefit assessment, or changes to the Reference Safety Information (RSI), are specified. Route B Streamlining: Route B substantial modifications are designated for automatic approval by the licensing authority, provided all changes qualify as Route B substantial modifications. Application Submission: Substantial modification applications for combined review should be submitted via the Integrated Research Application System (IRAS) or to the licensing authority and ethics committee separately. Decision Timelines: Confirmation of automatic approval for Route B modifications is issued within 14 calendar days of validation, while combined decisions take up to 35 calendar days. Title: Adversarial Machine Learning
Post Text: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Adversarial Machine Learning This guidance outlines the taxonomy of adversarial machine learning attacks, focusing on predictive, generative, and agentic systems, and details associated privacy compromises and system-level defenses. ML Attack Taxonomy: The taxonomy of machine learning attacks is categorized into Predictive ML Attacks, Generative SI Attacks, and Agentic SI Attacks. Predictive ML Attacks: This category includes Availability Violations, such as Model Poisoning, Data Poisoning, and Energy-latency attacks. Integrity Violations: Integrity violations within predictive attacks involve Clean-label Poisoning, Clean-label Backdoor, Evasion, Backdoor Poisoning, Targeted Poisoning, Black-box Evasion, Model Poisoning, and Model Poisoning. Privacy Compromises: Privacy compromises in predictive attacks involve Model Extraction, Reconstruction, Membership Inference, Property Inference, and Property Inference. Generative SI Attacks: Generative SI attacks include Availability Violations like Denial of Service and Increased Computation, and Integrity Violations like Data Poisoning. Agentic Attacks: Agentic attacks encompass categories such as Agent Hijacking, Indirect Prompt Injection, Memory Poisoning, Malicious Tools, and Malicious Agents. Agentic Workflow Stages: The agentic workflow involves stages like Planning and Execution, which are vulnerable to attacks that corrupt reasoning or tool selection. Agentic Attack Vectors: Attack vectors against agentic systems include Direct Prompting Attacks, Resource Exhaustion, Query Access, and Indirect Prompt Injection. System Defenses: System-level defenses, such as CaMeL and ACE, constrain agent architecture to prevent untrusted content from influencing actions. Guideline Purpose: The Classification Guidelines were formulated to guide economic operators in accurately determining the management attributes and management categories of ultrasound products for medical aesthetic use. Medical Device Definition: Ultrasound products are managed as medical devices if they achieve intended uses such as fat emulsification, scar repair, contour lifting, or skin tightening, based on their working principles. Category Determination Basis: Management categories are determined based on the product's working principle, technical parameters, and intended use. Key Technical Parameters: Ultrasonic intensity (Ispta), ultrasonic pressure (pr), and focal plane distance are key technical parameters used for classification. Parameter Standards: Standards such as YY 0592-2016 for HIFU and YY 0830-2011 for Superficial Tissue Ultrasound Therapy Equipment specify testing methods for parameters. Future Adjustments: The NMPA will track technological development and make timely adjustments to the guidelines as new technologies and products emerge. Title: Accelerated Approval
Post Text: FDA Accelerated Approval This provides clarity on the FDA's policy for requiring confirmatory trials to be underway before granting accelerated approval for drugs treating serious or life-threatening conditions. Accelerated Approval: Accelerated Approval allows the FDA to approve drugs based on early study results thought to be reasonably likely to predict a clinical benefit. Surrogate Endpoints: A surrogate endpoint is a marker, laboratory measurement, radiographic image, physical sign, or other measure thought to predict clinical benefit but is not itself a measure of clinical benefit. Intermediate Endpoints: Intermediate clinical endpoints are measures of a therapeutic effect considered reasonably likely to predict the clinical benefit of a drug, such as an effect on irreversible morbidity and mortality (IMM). Basis for Decision: The FDA bases its decision on the scientific support for the proposed surrogate or intermediate clinical endpoint. Study Adequacy: Studies demonstrating a drug's effect on a surrogate or intermediate clinical endpoint must be "adequate and well controlled" as required by the FD&C Act. Confirmatory Trials: Sponsors must conduct post-approval trials to verify the anticipated clinical benefit, and the FDA may require these trials to be underway before granting accelerated approval. Withdrawal of Approval: If post-market studies show the drug does not demonstrate clinical benefit, the FDA can withdraw approval using expedited procedures. Safety Standards: Drugs approved via accelerated approval must meet the same safety standards as all other FDA-approved drugs. Thank you for your time and please Like , Share, and/or Comment ...more
